quick-headline.heads_up: Neptune + GNN kept deliberately. CLAUDE.md records the graph neural network as SETTLED and in the headline, so 'walk me through the GNN architecture' is a certainty in any technical round for this seat. 'Multi-tenant SaaS + AI-powered systems' and the standalone 'LLM' segment were absorbed into 'AI-Native + Agentic Systems'; multi-tenancy still lives in Key Skills and in four Deque bullets. Model Context Protocol was deliberately NOT put in the headline — see quick-skills-ee.
quick-headline.hygiene: Tagline exception applies: SaaS, AI, GNN, HIPAA and ISO 27001 stay unexpanded here. AI is expanded on first use in the Summary immediately below; GNN is expanded in Key Skills; MCP is expanded in Key Skills.

Both are also in Key Skills. If he wants either as a bullet, the swap candidate is the Pioneered Context Graph line.
quick-summary.hygiene: A draft of this Summary named 'large language model narrative guardrails' and it was pulled before the file was finalised: whether those guardrails shipped is on the open confirm-or-reject list, and adding an open claim to the resume is his call, not a tailoring pass's. The master's own 'deterministic code owning every number' stands in its place. Key Skills still carries the master's 'LLM Productionisation (Guardrails, Field-Level Claim Grammar, Replay Determinism)' line unchanged, because that is the master's existing wording and the no-scrub rule applies to it. First-use expansions carried here: artificial intelligence (AI), Amazon Web Services (AWS), software as a service (SaaS). The master's 'shipped ten analytics...' opener was changed to 'Most recently ten...' — 'Shipped' leads an El Paso bullet and the master carried that collision. 'Cut infrastructure cost' became 'infrastructure cost down' — 'Cut' leads a Teletext bullet. 'inherits a fix rather than carrying its own copy' replaced 're-implementing it' — 'Implemented' leads a Deque bullet.

quick-skills-ee.why: Reordered so the first five lines are the JD's five technical must-haves in order: vector retrieval and semantic search, retrieval data access layers, agentic/LLM service interfaces, hands-on Python, query routing. quick-skills-ee.heads_up: MCP is placed HERE and nowhere else on purpose. CLAUDE.md lists 'real Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers' as safe to claim but records no project, scale or date for them. A skills label is a capability claim and is honest; putting MCP inside the Amura bullet would have invented a context the record does not support. Expect 'where did you build MCP servers?' and have the answer ready. Also dropped for this seat: Kinesis and ECS from the AWS line, the whole Datadog/Amplitude/ELK observability line, DevOps & CI/CD, Identity & Access, Statistical Rigor, and System Design at Scale. Kubernetes and Terraform were added to the AWS line.

First-use expansions now carried here: large language model (LLM), Model Context Protocol (MCP), Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), Application Programming Interfaces (APIs), Graph Neural Network (GNN), Command Query Responsibility Segregation (CQRS). quick-vp.why: Ten bullets down to seven, re-vectored end to end for this seat. In: Tuned (precedent retrieval, self-hosted SageMaker embedders, P99/NDCG), Assembled (the 10-query platform in Python — FastAPI, LangChain, LangGraph — on 4 reusable archetypes), Promoted (15 shared platform components, 14 landed, every query binding to the shared version), Pioneered (Context Graph + GNN), Brokered (company-wide adoption of Go, DynamoDB, Kubernetes, Terraform). Out: Architected (Kinesis shards), Scaled (Go chat concurrency), Deployed (Datadog), Delivered (patient onboarding), Drove (Claude Code rollout — moved to the Summary), Hardened, Extracted, Sequenced. Kept in place: Engineered (dense_vector RAG) and Secured (self-hosted models in-VPC), which are the two the JD asks for most directly.
quick-vp.heads_up: The Tuned bullet uses Variant B wording from master/merge_proposal.html — 'designed against warm-path P99 under 200 ms and 0.75 normalised discounted cumulative gain', not 'achieved'. Both figures are pre-registered Amura acceptance targets, and CLAUDE.md forbids presenting a target as a result. This matters more here than on any other seat, because that bullet is the single closest match to what this JD asks for; if he is asked about the numbers in a room, the honest answer is that they were the acceptance criteria the design was built to. The Engineered bullet keeps 'keeping Amazon Neptune off the serving path' — that phrasing is binding: KQ1's stack table makes Elasticsearch the authoritative serving index and puts Neptune deliberately off the serving path. Never let it be rewritten as retrieval running over Neptune. No Amura outcome metrics exist and none were invented.
quick-vp.hygiene: Five new leading verbs — Tuned, Assembled, Pioneered, Promoted, Brokered — each verified free across all ten roles including the five card-only pre-2016 ones, by stem grep across the whole file. Tuned's only hit is 'Neptune', a substring rather than a shared root, which CLAUDE.md explicitly permits. 'as platform standards' was chosen over 'as engineering standards' in the Brokered bullet because 'Engineered' leads bullet one. The Brokered bullet keeps '5 sub-teams' scoped to Go and DynamoDB only — CLAUDE.md attaches that count to those two, and Kubernetes/Terraform are confirmed company-wide but not to a sub-team count. The Pioneered bullet uses '10,000+ patients' rather than repeating '80+ chronic conditions' from bullet one. All seven at 25 words or fewer.

Added 'Exposed shared platform APIs to 20+ enterprise clients — Jira integration, API versioning, customer-specific frontends on one Spring Boot backend, backward compatibility' from the verified merge pool. It is the closest thing in his history to the JD's 'establishing technical standards adopted across multiple engineering teams' outside VoltusWave, and it is placed second for that reason. Steered and Forged were enriched in place from the same pool — Steered gains 'axe Monitor on Spring Boot 2.x and Java 8/17', Forged gains 'users, roles, clients, groups'.
quick-deque.heads_up: The 70-80% consolidation figure and 'approximately 300 enterprise instances' are both on the confirm-or-reject list and are untouched — only the surrounding detail changed. Do not let either be rewritten in a prep pass; they are his to settle.
quick-deque.hygiene: One new leading verb, Exposed, verified free across all ten roles. It uses the short form 'APIs' because Engineering Excellence now expands 'Application Programming Interfaces (APIs)' earlier in reading order. Championed moved above Productized so the architecture-decision bullet sits higher. All seven at 25 words or fewer.

quick-teletext.why: The single highest-leverage honest lift on this seat. The master framed the Artirix replacement purely as cost — 'retiring a third-party pricing product for an in-house ELK cache'. The journey doc (lines 422-425) records what it actually was: a cache-aside retrieval tier over Elasticsearch at 2-3 million requests per day, 20-minute TTL, with filtering, sorting and custom relevance ranking. Told as retrieval work, this converts one year of retrieval experience into roughly a decade, using work he already did, with no new claim.
quick-teletext.heads_up: 'third-party pricing product' became 'third-party search product'. Artirix was a search-technology company supplying the hotel pricing flow, so both descriptions are true; 'search' is the one that matches what he built. The Lifted bullet is untouched — it already carries the ranking and the 2-3 million daily requests, so bullet two does not repeat them. The +65% hotel conversions figure in that bullet remains unverified and remains on the resume per the no-scrub rule; it is his call, not a prep pass's.
quick-teletext.hygiene: Edited in place keeping the leading verb 'Cut', per Rule 7. 'ELK' replaced by 'Elasticsearch' — the observability line that expanded ELK left Key Skills for this seat, so the acronym had no first-use expansion left. 23 words.
